header.running_head: Rebuking and Advising Caution to those who Do Not Abstain from Worldly Luxuries and Who Indulge themselves

blocks.text: The Parting Advice Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) gave to Hadhrat Salmaan (RA)

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that he once went to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and asked for some advice. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Fear Allaah, O Salmaan! You should know that there will be many conquests. Your share from it should be only that (food) which you need for your stomach and that (clothing) which you need to cover yourself. You should also know that whoever performs his five salaahs is in the protection of Allaah in the mornings and in the evenings. You should also never kill anyone in Allaah's protection because you will then be breaching the security of Allaah because of which Allaah will throw you headlong into Jahannam."[^1]

Another narration from Hadhrat Hasan states that Hadhrat Salmaan Faarsi (RA) visited Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on his deathbed and asked, "Do give me some advice, O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Allaah shall open up the world to you so none of you should ever take more than what he needs just to get along."[^2]
The Parting Words Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) spoke to Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)

Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) once visited Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) on his deathbed and greeted him with Salaam. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Although it has not yet arrived, I can see worldly wealth approaching. It will however arrive and you people will then have curtains of silk and cushions of velvet. You will then (be so used to luxury that you will) experience difficulty using the woollen beddings of Azerbaijan, feeling as if you are lying on the thorns of the Su'daan tree. By Allaah! For one of you to be brought forward and executed is better for him than swimming in the intoxication of this world.[^3]
Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) Rebukes his Companions about their Lack of Abstinence and his Narration Concerning the Abstinence of Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Ali bin Rabaah narrates that he once heard Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) say, "You people spend the morning and the evenings hankering after that which Rasulullaah ﷺ abstained from. You have started hankering after the world when Rasulullaah ﷺ stayed away from it. By Allaah! Not a night passed Rasulullaah ﷺ in his entire life without his debts exceeding his dues." Some of the Sahabah (RA) then said, "We did see Rasulullaah ﷺ taking loans."[^4]
Ahmad in his Zuhd and Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.137), as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.8 Pg.233).
Deenowri, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.146).
Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.34). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.362).
Ahmad, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.5 Pg.166).
